source.title: Using Wavelets and Spectral Methods to Study Patterns in Image-Classification Datasets

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies spectral analysis to image datasets with correct, random, and partly random labels, measuring pattern-class association rather than whether a deep network fits those labels. Its results bear on V4's association-with-labels component, using a different method.
record.gate_note: Rows report this paper's own wavelet and spectral analysis of CIFAR-10 labels. Statements that deep networks can fit random labels or random-noise images are cited/background claims and are not rows. The analysis does not measure network training error, test error, training time, optimizer or regularizer effects, unstructured inputs, or the order in which networks learn patterns.
record.test_reason: The study measures dataset pattern–label associations using wavelets and spectral decomposition. It does not measure deep-network fitting, generalization under label corruption, or learning dynamics. Pattern–label association alone does not test V4. Neural-network fitting of random labels and noise inputs is cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that wavelet spectral decomposition extracts class-associated patterns and informative low-rank image reconstructions, and can reveal loss of pattern–class association under random labeling. They propose this as a tool for studying dataset learnability and memorization versus learning, without directly testing neural-network memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses wavelet transformation and higher-order generalized singular value decomposition to analyze dataset pattern-class associations; it does not train a network using the original intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Association changes with the fraction of random labels: the reported 20% random-label analysis resembles correct labels, while all-random labels produce near-zero angular distances for almost all patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Correct labels yield class-associated spectral patterns; fully random labels produce uniform class singular values and near-zero Ship–Truck angular distances. At 20% randomization, results resemble the correct-label analysis; other corruption fractions are described qualitatively as increasing disassociation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wavelet spectral decomposition detects dataset pattern–label associations that weaken as labels are randomized.

record.problems: The evidence on random labels is a spectral analysis of CIFAR-10 rather than a network fitting experiment. Results across corruption fractions are described qualitatively; only the 20% condition and all-random condition are specified here. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Network training error and chance test error under fully random labels with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Network fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect network training fit and steadily increasing test error across label-corruption fractions, including capture of remaining signal while memorizing noise.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats pattern–label association as a tested component of V4. None of the six versions names this dataset-level construct.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not train deep networks on random labels or report training/test error.
No training time or convergence speed is measured.
No network fitting of shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs is measured.

The paper measures whether patterns associate with labels at selected corruption levels, but does not measure network training error or test error across the full range from no corruption to all corruption.
No regularization or data augmentation conditions are compared.
No network training trajectory or order of learning real versus random labels is measured.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 dataset
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; dataset size not stated here
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-specific singular values with correct labels to assess pattern-class association.
rows.measure: Association of extracted patterns with classes, assessed through singular values.
rows.value: Patterns emerge that are associated with more than 1 class; Truck and Automobile have the highest singular values for many patterns.
rows.note: This is the correct-label reference analysis for pattern-class association; it does not evaluate network accuracy.
rows.check: The reported class-specific singular values describe correctly labeled CIFAR-10, not network training fit or test-error degradation. The qualitative value is consistent with Section 5.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 dataset
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; dataset size not stated here
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-specific singular values after randomizing labels for all images.
rows.measure: Association of extracted patterns with classes, assessed through singular values and angular distances.
rows.baseline: Correct-label results: patterns associated with classes; for Ship and Truck, angular distance is noticeable for many patterns.
rows.value: Singular values become uniform across classes; angular distances are close to zero for almost all patterns.
rows.locator: Section 5, Figures 7b and 8, and accompanying text
rows.note: Measures pattern-label disassociation, not perfect training fit or chance test error of a neural network.
rows.check: Uniform singular values and near-zero angular distances measure pattern–label disassociation, not network memorization or chance test performance. The angular-distance comparison specifically concerns Ship versus Truck.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 dataset
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; dataset size not stated here
rows.operation_detail: Repeated spectral analysis with 20% of labels randomized and correct labels retained for the rest.
rows.measure: Pattern-class association compared with the correctly labeled analysis.
rows.baseline: Results obtained for correctly labeled data.
rows.value: Results are not very different from those obtained for correctly labeled data.
rows.locator: Section 5, paragraph beginning “If we limit the portion”
rows.note: No numerical association measure or network error is reported for this corruption condition.
rows.check: Similarity to the correctly labeled spectral analysis at 20% randomization cannot establish partial network fitting or generalization. The reported qualitative value is accurate, but the original partial state is unsupported for V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
